recentItems.title: Cardinal says Pope Leo is in good shape prior to surgical intervention in lung
recentItems.description:
Cardinal Gérald Lacroix, archbishop of Quebec, said after the "A dieci anni di Amoris laetitia" event at Vatican's press office on Monday (October 12) that Pope Leo is in good shape prior to his surgical lung intervention for which the pontiff will be admitted to hospital on Tuesday.

He had announced after his weekly Angelus prayer on Sunday (October 11) that a small lung nodule had been found during a recent check-up, but described it as "well-contained" and said it had been spotted early.

The Vatican press office told journalists that the pope is expected to be hospitalized on late Tuesday morning, ahead of his surgery. It did not say when the actual operation would take place and added that the pope's recovery is expected to take about a week.

Leo, the leader of the 1.4-billion-member church, had several public appointments on his calendar for this week, including a mass in St. Peter's Square on Wednesday morning. The Vatican has not said if the mass, the closing event of a week-long assembly of bishops, will still be held. While the pope is going to hospital on Tuesday, it could still be led by a Vatican cardinal.

A nodule on the lung is a small, localized lesion that can be benign. The American Thoracic Society says fewer than 5% of lung nodules overall prove cancerous, although risk rises with age, size, and other factors such as smoking.

(Camera: Cristiano Corvino. Production, editing: Clara Schoenthaler. Writing: Joshua McElwee, Clara Schoenthaler)

recentItems.title: Pope Leo sticks to busy schedule before surgery to remove lung nodule
recentItems.description:
Pope Leo maintained his regular busy schedule on Monday (October 12) as he awaits surgery to remove a small growth found on one of his lungs, holding seven previously planned meetings in the morning, the Vatican said.

    The pontiff is expected to go into hospital on Tuesday (October 13) morning as he prepares for surgery to remove a nodule on one of his lungs.

    Leo, 71, said on Sunday (October 11) that the growth - a small nodule - had been found during recent check-up, but was "well-contained" and had been spotted early.

    The Vatican did not confirm when the surgery would take place.

(Production: Oriana Boselli)

recentItems.title: Leo Borromeo bags double gold at Makati Speedcubing Open IX
recentItems.description:
MANILA — Two-time Philippine Championship 4x4 champion and 2025 National 3x3 champion Leo Borromeo emerged victorious after claiming both titles at the Makati Speedcubing Open IX 2026 on Oct. 11 at SM Makati, after posting a 6.05-second average in the 3x3 event.

Borromeo finished ahead of the 12-year old speedcuber Juan Miguel "Uno" Magallanes, who recorded a 6.92-second average, while Gabriel Subion rounded out the podium with 7.64-second average for the main event, 3x3. 

The Cebuano speedcuber also bagged the 4x4 title with an average of 26-seconds, finishing ahead of CJ Garon, who posted a 29.13-second average, while Jhon Leinard Agcaoili settled for third, averaging 33.73 seconds.

Despite securing both titles, Borromeo said his main goal at the tournament was to experiment with techniques and become more comfortable competing, rather than focus on winning. 

He acknowledged that his finals performance fell short of his expectations but said the experience allowed him to learn lessons he hopes to apply in future tournaments.

"I didn't do that well to my standards in the finals, but it was enough to win. So, at least there's that," Borromeo admitted. 

He recorded a 5.2-seconds average during the second round of the 3x3 event, which he described as acceptable performance by his standards.

"Just to have fun and not overthink whenever I solve," he said.

Moving forward, Borromeo aims to participate in more competitions to become more comfortable in a competitive setting and achieve results he can be satisfied with.

"I just aim to go to more competitions, get used and comfortable in a competition setting, and hopefully I can have results that I can be happy with," he added.

recentItems.title: Competitive speedcubing gains traction in PH
recentItems.description:
MANILA — Competitive speedcubing continues to grow in the Philippines, with more than 6,000 registered competitors nationwide, according to World Cube Association (WCA) delegate, Yuji Yoshida. 

Speedcubing is the competitive practice of solving twisty puzzles, specifically Rubik's Cubes, in the shortest time possible. Unlike casual solving, competitions follow standardized rules and procedures, with results recorded on the WCA website. 

Speaking at the Makati Speedcubing Open IX 2026, Yoshida said the Philippine speedcubing community had expanded since the country's first WCA competition in 2007, with social media and local Rubik's Cube retailers helping introduce the sport to more people.

"I believe that we are over 6,000 registered competitors nationwide," he said, attributing the growth partly to organizers' social media activities and initiatives of local cube retailers.

Competitors participate in different events, including the 2x2, 3x3 and larger cubes as well as puzzles such as the Pyraminx and Megaminx. Each event requires specific solving techniques, which participants develop through practice, pattern recognition and memorized sequence of moves called algorithms. 

Competitions use specialized timers to record solved times, while judges oversee attempts to ensure that participants follow the rules. Depending on the event, results may be based on individual solves or averages calculated from multiple attempts.

Under the standard average-of-five format, the fastest and slowest times are removed before the remaining three are averaged. Competitors may also receive penalties or a "Did Not Finish" result for certain mistakes or rule violations, depending on the applicable regulations.

"The responsibility of the delegate is to oversee the competition, make sure that all of the rules are followed, even by the first-time competitors," Yoshida said. 

He added that orientations are conducted before competitions to familiarize participants with the rules and procedures. 

Yoshida, who has served as a delegate for more than three years and overseen over 100 competitions nationwide, said participants can approach him if they encounter problems during an event.

Beyond competition rankings, Yoshida said personal improvement is a major motivation for speedcubers. Their results are recorded on the WCA website, allowing them to track their performances and aim for faster times in subsequent competitions.

He added that the community's accessibility contributes to its appeal, particularly among younger participants and students.

"The Rubik's Cube itself, you can just carry it around everywhere, you can practice everywhere without electricity," Yoshida said.

Yoshida also described the community as welcoming, saying that participants continue to return as competitions provide opportunities to improve their personal records. 

"If they fail to do so, there's always next time," he added.

With more competitions being held nationwide and increased visibility through social media, Philippine speedcubing continues to provide participants with opportunities to develop their skills, track their progress and compete against others while pursuing their personal bests.
